name: TestSwitchNetworkInstanceSuite/TestSwitchNIDeletedWithAppsAttached
statusMessage:
timed out after 5m0.000767114s (excluding download) waiting for app "ac3840d3-d24b-4f12-b080-774fd32ae3d0" (app-1) on device "edge-dev" to reach RUNNING state (last state: RESOLVING_TAG)

Claude's conclusion:
### Root cause

Live evidence confirms this is the same known "hung image tag-resolve" family already documented in the ledger, but with a new detail that pins down the actual mechanism. `app-1`'s content tree (`0ff24197-...`, image `lfedge/evetest-ubuntu-ctr:1.2`) and `app-2`'s sibling request both started their `handleResolveCreate` calls concurrently at 23:27:30. `app-2` resolved normally ~3 minutes later (23:30:26, `State:108`), but `app-1`'s resolve made no further progress for the full 5-minute test window (`/run/downloader/ResolveStatus/` was empty the whole time — no persisted resolve status, matching the "vanished" signature from past occurrences). Checking back live, `app-1` did eventually recover: `evetest eve app-info` shows an explicit app error fired at 23:37:30 — `"no response from the transport for lfedge/evetest-ubuntu-ctr:1.2 in 10m0.000431206s, cancelling"` — after which the retry succeeded immediately and the app progressed through INSTALLED → BOOTING → RUNNING by 23:38:37. So the resolve wasn't actually hung forever, it was blocked on a 10-minute internal transport timeout (go-containerregistry `remote.Get` call) that is more than double the test's 5-minute wait, guaranteeing a timeout regardless.

This is a known, recurring issue per `live-ledger.md`: the identical "one of two concurrent tag-resolve requests stalls while the sibling resolves quickly" signature for this exact test (`TestSwitchNIDeletedWithAppsAttached`) was first seen 2026-11-02, and the same downloader/resolve-hang mechanism has recurred repeatedly since (including `TestFlowLog`/`acl-app` variants). Tonight's occurrence adds new evidence not previously captured — the actual 10-minute transport-timeout/cancel/retry cycle — pinpointing that the root bug is an excessively long internal transport timeout in the OCI registry resolve path rather than a true infinite hang. The broker host is fairly loaded (99% of host memory committed to running VMs, load ~4-6 on 32 CPUs) but not obviously overloaded, so this looks like the long-standing code-level issue rather than a new infra-contention cause. No PR diff was supplied, so no relatedness verdict applies.
